title: Can quantum-mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?
text:
Abstract
In a complete theory there is an element corresponding to each element of reality. A sufficient condition for the reality of a physical quantity is the possibility of predicting it with certainty, without disturbing the system. In quantum mechanics in the case of two physical quantities described by non-commuting operators, the knowledge of one precludes the knowledge of the other. Then either (1) the description of reality given by the wave function in quantum mechanics is not complete or (2) these two quantities cannot have simultaneous reality. Consideration of the problem of making predictions concerning a system on the basis of measurements made on another system that had previously interacted with it leads to the result that if (1) is false then (2) is also false. One is thus led to conclude that the description of reality as given by a wave function is not complete.

title: Richard Liu

Thanks for stopping by!
I’m Richard Liu, a Ph.D. trainee at NYU Grossman School of Medicine, supervised by Dr. Ivan Diaz. I’m fortunate to collaborate with researchers including Dr. Wenbo Wu, Dr. Kara Rudolph, Dr. Michele Santacatterina, and Dr. Alex Luedtke. I also work as a research assistant with Dr. David M. Charytan and Dr. Jiyuan Hu, among others.
I’m, in general, interested in developing and applying modern statistical and machine learning methods to questions in public health and medicine. My research focuses on causal machine learning, semiparametric theory, mediation analysis, and causal inference with time-varying treatments and outcomes. I’ve also worked on projects involving transportability, causal fairness, and applications of large language models (LLMs) to causal inference.
Outside of research, I am also interested in a lot of activities, including cooking, exercising, including fitness training and archery, and playing card and video games.
Please feel free to reach out if you’re interested in collaborating!
